title: Doctrine sends every file-touching request through a brief and an approval, at every lane
action: Make the written workflow match D1 and D6: every request that writes a file gets a brief and an approval moment, at EVERY lane. Two edits, both in doctrine, no Rust. FIRST, the routing table in skills/bee-hive/references/routing-and-contracts.md currently sends 'Just fix this / small change' straight to bee-planning, which is why bee-shaping's Lock never runs for tiny and small and no CONTEXT.md is ever written for them. Reroute so those requests reach a brief first. Keep the ceremony proportionate per D1: tiny and small earn a SHORT brief, not the full standard treatment, and lanes keep their current plan ceremony — D1 adds a brief and a recorded approval, never plan ceremony. SECOND, the ceremony table in the same file lists Gate 1 as a human stop only for standard and high-risk. Make the approval moment exist at every code-touching lane including docs, and state plainly that gate_bypass decides whether the run STOPS, never whether the record EXISTS (per D2) — an auto-approved run still writes its brief and its approval record, stamped actor auto with the bypass level and reason, which the CLI now supports since trun-2. Update skills/bee-hive/references/gates-and-delegation.md wherever it describes what bypass skips, so the two files cannot disagree. Also state the D6 boundary explicitly: a request that writes a file is in scope, code and docs alike; a pure question that changes nothing on disk is not, and creates no record. Say what a tiny or docs brief actually IS and where it lives — if a short CONTEXT.md is the answer, say so in one line; do not invent a new artifact type without saying where it is written. AFTER editing, run the regen chain from the repo root: `bee dev regen` (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write). It stops at the first red with that step named. A doctrine edit that skips regen ships a stale rendered tree, and CI drift-checks it. The cell store also requires, for any cell touching skills/: run `bee dev release-manifest --check` as part of verify and treat docs/history/codex-harness-hardening/release-manifest.json as a file you may write — `bee dev regen`'s release-manifest --write step updates it, so commit that update with your change.

truths: The routing table sends a small or tiny file-touching request through a brief before planning, not straight to planning
The ceremony table shows an approval moment at every code-touching lane, docs included
The doctrine states that gate_bypass decides whether the run stops, never whether the brief and approval record exist
The doctrine states the D6 boundary: a file write is in scope, code and docs alike; a pure question creates no record
The doctrine names what a tiny or docs brief is and the path it is written to
bee dev regen completes green after the edits

artifacts.substantive: routing and ceremony tables rewritten for a brief and an approval at every lane, with proportionate ceremony
bypass description aligned so it scopes the stop, not the record

key_links: the ceremony table and the bypass table agree on what an auto-approved run still records
prohibitions: No Rust changes in this cell
No added plan ceremony for tiny or small — a brief and an approval record only
No new artifact type introduced without naming the path it is written to
No edit to CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md

trace.outcome: Doctrine now sends every file-touching request through a brief and an approval at every lane

report.outcome: Rerouted tiny/small/docs requests through a short brief (Lock writes a short CONTEXT.md) before planning or a docs write, added Gate 1 to the docs lane, and stated that gate_bypass scopes the stop not the record (D2) with the actual --actor/--bypass-level/--reason flags; aligned gates-and-delegation.md so bypass never skips brief authoring or the approval record. Ran bee dev regen (all 3 steps green) and committed the resulting release-manifest and rendered-tree updates.
